title: Imaging and Stimulating Enteric Neurons in the Murine Large Intestine
author: Dante Heredia
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.82fhybn
materials: Nikon Eclipse FN1 upright fluorescence microscope

steps.title: Excise colon into oxygenated dish
steps.instruction: Make a ventral midline incision, remove the whole colon, and place it in a Sylguard‑lined dissection dish containing oxygenated Krebs‑Ringer solution.

steps.title: Flatten colon sheet
steps.instruction: Using scissors, cut along the mesenteric border until the tubular colon opens into a flat sheet.

steps.title: Pin tissue and place electrodes
steps.instruction: Pin the region of interest (proximal, middle, or distal) mucosal side down; pin the end sections of the proximal and distal regions mucosal side up for brush stimulation, and lay two platinum electrode wires across the serosal layer in a perpendicular orientation.

steps.title: Configure imaging system
steps.instruction: Set up a Nikon Eclipse FN1 upright fluorescence microscope with a Nikon Plan Fluor 20× lens; connect a Photometrics Prime 95B sCMOS camera and a Windows PC running Nikon NIS‑Elements 4.1; record image sequences at 25 frames per second.

steps.title: Perfuse with oxygenated solution
steps.instruction: Continuously perfuse the preparation with oxygenated Krebs‑Ringer solution maintained at 36–37 °C.

steps.title: Apply mucosal and electrical stimulation
steps.instruction: Perform mucosal stimulation with a camel‑hair paintbrush (five brush strokes in ~5 seconds) and apply electronic field stimulation at 20 Hz for 10 seconds using 6 V, 0.01 ms pulse duration.

substeps.instruction: Brush stimulation: five strokes in ~5 s with camel‑hair brush.
Field stimulation: 20 Hz, 10 s, 6 V, 0.01 ms pulses.
